The small size is a rare engineering-loot find, usually broken; the medium and large sizes are too big to turn up in salvage. The K-Leg fixer buys them back intact and the Venus scrap kiosk intact or broken. Also sold for scrip at the CCRE and GalCon faction kiosks; they ask Friendly standing.
groups.notes: Damaged, a store leaks to space (about 2, 3 or 4 kg an hour by size) until repaired. With oxygen in the room and a fire, a working V4 hearth or a sparking damaged device, its contents burn: the room loses oxygen and warms, and the game's own explosion follows. Dismantling refuses while it holds hydrogen.

groups.title: K2 Sabatier Reactor
groups.function: A 2 x 2 catalytic Sabatier reactor, CO2 + 4 H2 -> CH4 + 2 H2O. Each one-hour cycle at 1.2 kW takes 0.125 kg of hydrogen (one X2 cycle) and 0.682 kg of CO2 and makes 0.559 kg of water and 0.249 kg of methane. The reaction and its electricity put about 2.3 kW into the room. Since Manufacturing 0.53.0, with a carbon monoxide store chosen as its carbon source it runs CO + 3 H2 -> CH4 + H2O instead: 0.125 kg of hydrogen and 0.579 kg of carbon monoxide into 0.332 kg of methane and 0.372 kg of water a cycle, with about 2.6 kW into the room.
groups.use: Install through APPS within one tile of an H2 store, an installed native CO2 canister, a water vessel (S3 or R3) and an M2 methane store; connect power; link all four on its panel or C1; Start. Fill the CO2 canister with the game's CO2 scrubber. For a CR-4's gas, choose a carbon monoxide store under CO2 or carbon monoxide from instead of a canister. It waits, with the reason, while an input is short or an output full, and starts a new cycle only once the last cycle's products are delivered.
groups.find: Buy loose hardware from the sellers below; it is late-game equipment with late-game prices. No fabrication recipe. About one engineering-loot roll in twenty yields a Fennmark machine, usually broken; see the exact offers below. The K-Leg fixer buys it back intact and the Venus scrap kiosk intact or broken. Also sold for scrip at the CCRE and GalCon faction kiosks; they ask Trusted standing.
groups.notes: With the X2 it returns about half the water the X2 splits, as NASA's ISS system does. Damaged, it dumps the gas it holds: CO2, carbon monoxide and methane into the room, and its hydrogen burns if the room has oxygen and a spark, otherwise it escapes; water stays in its hold. It carries on after a reload if it was running. Dismantling refuses while it holds gas, water or a part-run cycle.

groups.title: AX-2 Ammonia Cracker
groups.function: A 2 x 2 catalytic ammonia cracker from Tolvane, a new brand for the nitrogen line: each one-hour cycle at 2 kW splits 1 kg of ammonia into 0.822 kg of nitrogen and 0.178 kg of hydrogen (2 NH3 -> N2 + 3 H2).
groups.use: Install through APPS within one tile of an ammonia store, a nitrogen store and a hydrogen store (any sizes), connect power, set Ammonia from, Nitrogen to and Hydrogen to on its panel or C1, then Start. It works only when both product stores have room for a whole cycle. About 1.25 kW warms the room while it works. See [the player guide](manufacturing-player-guide.md).
groups.find: Buy loose hardware from the sellers below; it is late-game equipment with late-game prices. No fabrication recipe. About one engineering-loot roll in twenty yields a Manufacturing machine, usually broken; see the exact offers below. The K-Leg fixer buys it back intact and the Venus scrap kiosk intact or broken. Also sold for scrip at the CCRE and GalCon faction kiosks; they ask Trusted standing.
groups.notes: It carries on after a reload if it was running. A damaged or destroyed cracker releases the ammonia and nitrogen it holds into the room and its hydrogen burns or escapes; it holds at most one cycle. Complete conversion is an authored simplification.

groups.title: LC-3 Leach and Crystallise Unit
groups.function: A 3 x 3 leach tank and closed crystalliser from Lixivar, a new brand for hydrometallurgy. The crew chooses one of six recipes at 12 kW: an evaporite crust in 20 kg of circulating water to 0.70 kg of potassium sulfate, 0.25 kg of phosphate concentrate, a 6.8 kg leached residue and a 2.25 kg brine salt cake (one hour; the water comes back); a phosphate concentrate with 30 g of ammonia and 0.22 kg of water to 0.43 kg of struvite and 70 g of caustic remainder (five minutes); with Phobos Agriculture, one potassium sulfate and two struvite to 39 Groundwork makeup salts packets (two and a half minutes); one of the game's olivine chunks with 8.64 kg of sulfuric acid and 9.52 kg of water to 32 Epsom salt and a 14.33 kg olivine leach cake (one hour, about 1.3 kWh of reaction heat into the room); one phosphoric acid flask and three Epsom salt with 0.27 kg of ammonia to three struvite, three ammonium sulfate and 94 g of water back to the vessel (ten minutes); and, with Agriculture 0.27.0 or newer, one each of potassium sulfate, struvite, Epsom salt and ammonium sulfate with 0.25 kg of ammonia and 0.73 kg of acid to 2.77 kg of crop nutrients in a linked nutrient hopper (five minutes). Since Manufacturing 0.52.0 it also turns three ferrosilicon and 3.02 kg of water into 0.339 kg of hydrogen for a linked hydrogen store, leaving three spent ferrosilicon (twenty minutes, about 7.9 kWh of reaction heat into the room).
groups.use: Install through APPS within one tile of a water vessel (S3 or R3) and, as the recipes need them, an ammonia store, an acid tank, a hydrogen store and a Groundwork nutrient hopper; connect power; on its panel or C1 link them and choose the recipe; load that recipe's charge into its feed (the Inventory opens the tray and the feed), then Start. It works the next charge of the same recipe when one is in the feed. Change the recipe only while no charge is bound. See [the player guide](manufacturing-player-guide.md).
groups.find: Buy loose hardware from the sellers below; it is late-game equipment with late-game prices. No fabrication recipe. About one engineering-loot roll in twenty yields a Manufacturing machine, usually broken; see the exact offers below. The K-Leg fixer buys it back intact and the Venus scrap kiosk intact or broken. Also sold for scrip at the CCRE and GalCon faction kiosks; they ask Trusted standing.
groups.notes: A charge that was running carries on after a reload. Nothing melts or spoils in it, and it breathes nothing into the room; 15 percent of its electricity warms the room. The crust's and the olivine's make-up, the Epsom yield, the blend's nitrogen level and the recipes' energies are authored; the reactions and sources are in the refinery design record. Empty the tray by hand.

groups.title: SA-3 Sulfuric Acid Plant
groups.function: A 3 x 3 roaster, converter bed and absorption tower from Lixivar. Each one-hour charge at 4 kW roasts one sulfide nodule in 6.28 kg of oxygen with 1.58 kg of water into 7.81 kg of sulfuric acid for a linked acid tank, a 0.515 kg phosphoric acid flask and 9.535 kg of roasted calcine. The reactions release about 21 kWh a nodule into the room.
groups.use: Install through APPS within one tile of an oxygen store, a water vessel and an acid tank; connect power; link all three on its panel or C1; load nodules into its feed (it holds two), then Start. Give it a large, cooled room: it waits whenever the room would pass 40 C. See [the player guide](manufacturing-player-guide.md).
groups.find: Buy loose hardware from the sellers below; it is late-game equipment with late-game prices. No fabrication recipe. About one engineering-loot roll in twenty yields a Manufacturing machine, usually broken; see the exact offers below. The K-Leg fixer buys it back intact and the Venus scrap kiosk intact or broken. Also sold for scrip at the CCRE and GalCon faction kiosks; they ask Trusted standing.
groups.notes: A charge that was running carries on after a reload. It breathes nothing into the room, but its heat is real and, like every Phobos machine, it does not work in vacuum. The nodule's make-up and the plant's energy are authored; the reactions and sources are in the refinery design record.

groups.title: EC-4 Electrolysis Cell
groups.function: A 4 x 4 molten-rock electrolysis cell from Oxsmith, a new brand for high-temperature oxygen plant. At 60 kW it melts one charge and splits it with current: a 20 kg lump of the game's loose regolith gives 3.9 kg of oxygen for a linked oxygen store, 0.4 kg of water for a linked water vessel, three ferrosilicon and nine refinery slag in an hour; a 10 kg chunk of the game's Silicates ore gives 2.6 kg of oxygen, two ferrosilicon and three slag in forty minutes. It uses no reagents. About half of what it draws warms the room, and a lump lets 0.1 kg of carbon dioxide into the air.
groups.use: Install through APPS with its back to a powered wall row, touching an oxygen store and a water vessel or joined to them by gas and water line; link both on its panel or C1; load loose regolith or Silicates ore into its Inventory (the feed holds two), then Start. It chooses the charge from what is loaded. Optional: a material bin under Take feed from, and a crate under Send products to. See [the player guide](manufacturing-player-guide.md).
groups.find: Buy loose hardware from the sellers below; it is late-game equipment with late-game prices. No fabrication recipe. About one engineering-loot roll in twenty yields a Manufacturing machine, usually broken; see the exact offers below. The K-Leg fixer buys it back intact and the Venus scrap kiosk intact or broken. Also sold for scrip at the CCRE and GalCon faction kiosks; they ask Trusted standing.
groups.notes: A charge that was running carries on after a reload. A cell kept waiting for a cooler room freezes and melts again with nothing lost. While working it can light a leaking fuel store in its room, like the refinery, and like every Phobos machine it does not work in vacuum. Not a way to make money: oxygen sells back at 45 percent and ferrosilicon is worth 2 cr, so a lump's products never repay the lump, and Silicates ore sells for far more raw. NASA Kennedy Space Center has demonstrated molten regolith electrolysis on lunar material; the lump's make-up, the yield, the hour and the 60 kW are authored. Sources are in the oxygen-from-rock design record.

groups.title: CR-4 Carbothermal Reactor
groups.function: A 4 x 4 reactor from Oxsmith that reduces molten rock with methane. At 30 kW, half the EC-4's draw, a 20 kg lump of the game's loose regolith takes 3.91 kg of methane from a linked store and gives 6.83 kg of carbon monoxide, 0.98 kg of hydrogen and 0.4 kg of water to linked stores, with three ferrosilicon and nine refinery slag, in an hour; a 10 kg chunk of Silicates ore takes 2.61 kg of methane and gives 4.55 kg of carbon monoxide, 0.65 kg of hydrogen, two ferrosilicon and three slag in forty minutes. A K2 with the carbon monoxide store as its carbon source turns the gas back into methane and water, and an X2 splits that water: about 3.9 kg of oxygen a lump, with the methane and hydrogen returned.
groups.use: Install through APPS with its back to a powered wall row, touching a methane store, a carbon monoxide store, a hydrogen store and a water vessel or joined to them by gas and water line; link all four on its panel or C1; load loose regolith or Silicates ore into its Inventory (the feed holds two), then Start. It waits, with the reason, until the methane store holds enough and the others have room. Optional: a material bin under Take feed from, and a crate under Send products to. See [the player guide](manufacturing-player-guide.md).
groups.find: Buy loose hardware from the sellers below; it is late-game equipment with late-game prices. No fabrication recipe. About one engineering-loot roll in twenty yields a Manufacturing machine, usually broken; see the exact offers below. The K-Leg fixer buys it back intact and the Venus scrap kiosk intact or broken. Also sold for scrip at the CCRE and GalCon faction kiosks; they ask Trusted standing.
groups.notes: A charge that was running carries on after a reload, and a waiting reactor loses nothing. While working it can light a leaking fuel store in its room, and like every Phobos machine it does not work in vacuum. Not cheaper to run than the EC-4: about 68 kWh a lump across the reactor, the K2 and the X2, and one K2 needs about twelve hours for a lump's gas; it is cheaper to buy and draws half the power at once. Not a way to make money. NASA's Carbothermal Reduction Demonstration at Johnson Space Center extracts oxygen from lunar regolith simulant as carbon monoxide; our reactor is about eight times as efficient as that test rig, and the yield, the hour and the 30 kW are authored. Sources are in the oxygen-from-rock design record.

groups.title: M2, M3 and M4 Methane Stores
groups.function: Passive pressurised stores for Sabatier methane (160, 395 and 770 kg), kept as a kilogram record, and a source of RCS propellant. Three sizes: small 2 x 2, medium 3 x 3 and large 4 x 4, each one tile wider and holding more for less per kilogram.
groups.use: Install through APPS within one tile of a K2 and link it from the reactor. Vent overboard or pour into another store of the same gas (within one tile or along a gas line) from its panel or C1. Repair damage at once and empty it before uninstalling. It feeds the RCS through a P1 manifold (within one tile or by gas line; switched off until you turn it on).
groups.find: Buy loose hardware from the sellers below; it is late-game equipment with late-game prices, and the bigger sizes cost less per kilogram held. No fabrication recipe. The small size is a rare engineering-loot find, usually broken; the medium and large sizes are too big to turn up in salvage. The K-Leg fixer buys them back intact and the Venus scrap kiosk intact or broken. Also sold for scrip at the CCRE and GalCon faction kiosks; they ask Friendly standing.
groups.notes: Methane is one of the game's own gases: a damaged store leaks about 2, 3 or 4 kg an hour into the room (to space where there is no air) until repaired, and a destroyed one releases what it held. With oxygen in the room and a fire, a working V4 hearth or a sparking damaged device, its contents burn, using 4 kg of oxygen and leaving 2.7 kg of CO2 per kg of methane, with the game's own explosion. Dismantling refuses while it holds methane.

groups.title: O2, O3 and O4 Oxygen Stores
groups.function: Passive pressurised stores for bulk oxygen (340, 840 and 1,630 kg), kept as a kilogram record. Three sizes: small 2 x 2, medium 3 x 3 and large 4 x 4, each one tile wider and holding more for less per kilogram.
groups.use: Install through APPS. Fill it from an X2 (choose the store as the cell's oxygen destination) or buy bulk oxygen at a station's Bulk supplies. It feeds an L2 filling station, which tops up canisters and suit bottles, and the RCS through a P1 manifold. Vent overboard or pour into another store of the same gas (within one tile or along a gas line) from its panel or C1. Repair damage at once and empty it before uninstalling.
groups.find: Buy loose hardware from the sellers below; it is late-game equipment with late-game prices, and the bigger sizes cost less per kilogram held. No fabrication recipe. The small size is a rare engineering-loot find, usually broken; the medium and large sizes are too big to turn up in salvage. The K-Leg fixer buys them back intact and the Venus scrap kiosk intact or broken. Also sold for scrip at the CCRE and GalCon faction kiosks; they ask Friendly standing.
groups.notes: Oxygen is one of the game's own gases: a damaged store leaks about 2, 3 or 4 kg an hour into the room until repaired, and a destroyed one releases what it held. Oxygen-rich air makes any fire worse. Bought oxygen costs the refuelling kiosk's own price per kilogram, and the kiosk buys stored oxygen back at 45% of it.

groups.title: N2, N3 and N4 Nitrogen Stores
groups.function: Passive pressurised stores for bulk nitrogen (300, 745 and 1,440 kg), kept as a kilogram record. Three sizes: small 2 x 2, medium 3 x 3 and large 4 x 4, each one tile wider and holding more for less per kilogram.
groups.use: Install through APPS and buy bulk nitrogen at a station's Bulk supplies, or fill it from an AX-2 ammonia cracker within one tile. It feeds an L2 filling station, which refills RCS and air-pump canisters far from port, and the RCS directly through a P1 manifold. Vent overboard or pour into another store of the same gas (within one tile or along a gas line) from its panel or C1. Repair damage at once and empty it before uninstalling.
groups.find: Buy loose hardware from the sellers below; it is late-game equipment with late-game prices, and the bigger sizes cost less per kilogram held. No fabrication recipe. The small size is a rare engineering-loot find, usually broken; the medium and large sizes are too big to turn up in salvage. The K-Leg fixer buys them back intact and the Venus scrap kiosk intact or broken. Also sold for scrip at the CCRE and GalCon faction kiosks; they ask Friendly standing.
groups.notes: Nitrogen is one of the game's own gases: a damaged store leaks about 2, 3 or 4 kg an hour into the room until repaired, thinning the air without warning, and a destroyed one releases what it held. Bought nitrogen costs the refuelling kiosk's own price per kilogram, and the kiosk buys stored nitrogen back at 45% of it.

groups.title: C2, C3 and C4 Carbon Dioxide Stores
groups.function: Passive pressurised stores for bulk carbon dioxide (470, 1,160 and 2,260 kg), kept as a kilogram record. Three sizes: small 2 x 2, medium 3 x 3 and large 4 x 4, each one tile wider and holding more for less per kilogram.
groups.use: Install through APPS and buy bulk carbon dioxide at a station's Bulk supplies. A K2 draws its CO2 from one within one tile (choose it as the reactor's CO2 source); it also feeds an L2 filling station for CO2 canisters and the RCS through a P1 manifold. Vent overboard or pour into another store of the same gas (within one tile or along a gas line) from its panel or C1. Repair damage at once and empty it before uninstalling.
groups.find: Buy loose hardware from the sellers below; it is late-game equipment with late-game prices, and the bigger sizes cost less per kilogram held. No fabrication recipe. The small size is a rare engineering-loot find, usually broken; the medium and large sizes are too big to turn up in salvage. The K-Leg fixer buys them back intact and the Venus scrap kiosk intact or broken. Also sold for scrip at the CCRE and GalCon faction kiosks; they ask Friendly standing.
groups.notes: Carbon dioxide is one of the game's own gases and poisons the crew: a damaged store leaks about 2, 3 or 4 kg an hour into the room until repaired, and a destroyed one releases what it held. Bought CO2 costs the game's own price per kilogram, and the kiosk buys stored CO2 back at 45% of it.

groups.title: Q2, Q3 and Q4 Ammonia Stores
groups.function: Passive pressurised stores for liquefied ammonia (380, 940 and 1,820 kg), kept as a kilogram record. Three sizes: small 2 x 2, medium 3 x 3 and large 4 x 4, each one tile wider and holding more for less per kilogram.
groups.use: Install through APPS within one tile of a V4 and choose it under the refinery's Send ammonia to; the salt crust charge will not start without one. An AX-2 cracker splits it into nitrogen and hydrogen, or the RCS can burn it through a P1 manifold, at about 1.41 times nitrogen's push per kilogram. Vent overboard or pour into another ammonia store (within one tile or along a gas line) from its panel or C1. Repair damage at once and empty it before uninstalling.
groups.find: Buy loose hardware from the sellers below; it is late-game equipment with late-game prices, and the bigger sizes cost less per kilogram held. No fabrication recipe. The small size is a rare engineering-loot find, usually broken; the medium and large sizes are too big to turn up in salvage. The K-Leg fixer buys them back intact and the Venus scrap kiosk intact or broken. Also sold for scrip at the CCRE and GalCon faction kiosks; they ask Friendly standing.
groups.notes: Ammonia is one of the game's own gases and poisons the crew: a damaged store leaks about 2, 3 or 4 kg an hour into the room until repaired, and a destroyed one releases what it held. Stations do not sell ammonia; it comes only from the salt crust. The refuelling kiosk buys stored ammonia at 45% of the game's ammonia price.

groups.title: Z2, Z3 and Z4 Carbon Monoxide Stores
groups.function: Passive pressurised stores for carbon monoxide (300, 745 and 1,440 kg), kept as a kilogram record. Three sizes: small 2 x 2, medium 3 x 3 and large 4 x 4, each one tile wider and holding more for less per kilogram. Red domes.
groups.use: Install through APPS touching a CR-4 or on its gas line and choose it under the reactor's Carbon monoxide to; then choose it on a K2 under CO2 or carbon monoxide from, and the K2 turns the gas and hydrogen into methane and water. A P1 manifold can burn it in the RCS as cold gas, worth what nitrogen is. Vent overboard or pour into another carbon monoxide store (within one tile or along a gas line) from its panel or C1. Repair damage at once and empty it before uninstalling.
groups.find: Buy loose hardware from the sellers below; it is late-game equipment with late-game prices, and the bigger sizes cost less per kilogram held. No fabrication recipe. The small size is a rare engineering-loot find, usually broken; the medium and large sizes are too big to turn up in salvage. The K-Leg fixer buys them back intact and the Venus scrap kiosk intact or broken. Also sold for scrip at the CCRE and GalCon faction kiosks; they ask Friendly standing.
groups.notes: Carbon monoxide is one of the game's own gases: it poisons the crew with no smell to warn them, and it burns. A damaged store leaks about 2, 3 or 4 kg an hour into the room until repaired, and a destroyed one releases what it held; with oxygen and something to light it, the contents burn into carbon dioxide instead. Stations do not sell carbon monoxide; it comes only from a CR-4. The refuelling kiosk buys it at 45% of the game's carbon monoxide price, which is very little. The L2 does not bottle it.

groups.title: AT-2, AT-3 and AT-4 Sulfuric Acid Tanks
groups.function: Bunded tanks for concentrated sulfuric acid, kept as a kilogram record: 1,150 kg in the 2 x 2 AT-2, 2,850 kg in the 3 x 3 AT-3 and 5,520 kg in the 4 x 4 AT-4. Liquid tanks, not gas stores: no gas line and no feed to thrusters, filling stations or cabin air.
groups.use: Install through APPS touching an SA-3 (which fills it) or an LC-3 (which draws from it), or join them with acid line laid under or right beside both; link it from those machines. Buy acid into it at a station's Bulk supplies. Pour acid into another tank it touches or shares an acid line with, from its panel or C1. Empty it before moving or dismantling it. Since Manufacturing 0.25.0 each tank has a four-place rack for Framework drain canisters: a canister of acid put in it pours into the tank.
groups.find: Buy loose hardware from the sellers below; it is late-game equipment with late-game prices, and the bigger sizes cost less per kilogram held. No fabrication recipe. The small size is a rare engineering-loot find, usually broken; the medium and large sizes are too big to turn up in salvage. The K-Leg fixer buys them back intact and the Venus scrap kiosk intact or broken. Also sold for scrip at the CCRE and GalCon faction kiosks; they ask Friendly standing.
groups.notes: Damaged, the bund holds the acid but a ten-thousandth of it reaches the room as the game's own sulfuric acid mist, which poisons in its bands; repair, then recover the acid. A destroyed tank mists the same share and the rest is lost. A wet acid line that is damaged spills about a kilogram from the tank feeding it into this bund. Bought acid costs the game's own 3.1 cr/kg, and the kiosk buys stored acid back at 45% of it.

groups.title: Lixivar acid line
groups.function: Lined line for concentrated sulfuric acid between the AT acid tanks and the machines that fill or draw from them: the SA-3 and the LC-3. Every acid tank, SA-3 and LC-3 the line runs under or right beside joins one network, and touching equipment joins without it. It has its own violet lane, so it shares tiles with other lines.
groups.use: Lay it through INSTALL > HVAC on intact floor until it runs under or right beside each machine and tank, on any side. Then link the machine to the tank on its Control Panel; the list shows how each tank is reached. To take it up, right-click it and choose Drain line into canister with a Framework drain canister carried or within two tiles; the run closes until Return line to service.
groups.find: Sold new at the K-Leg supply kiosk and fixer, San Diego Halvorson and the Venus scrap kiosk in lots of 128. Ordinary supply. Also sold for scrip at the CCRE and GalCon faction kiosks, at any standing.
groups.notes: New in Manufacturing 0.24.0. Since Manufacturing 0.25.0 it holds about 0.9 kg of acid a tile, filled from its tanks (an authored metre of 25 mm bore), and a segment holding acid cannot be taken up until drained. Damaged or destroyed, a segment lets a ten-thousandth of what it holds into the room as mist; a damaged one keeps the rest until drained. Dismantling returns only retained waste, which is terminal.

groups.title: Alembrine Copperhead-3 Fermenter-Still
groups.function: A 3 x 3, 3 kW fermenter and pot still: six of Phobos Agriculture's sugar beets or six beet sugar packets a charge, into ethanol for a Cask tank, carbon dioxide for a store and water for a silo.
groups.use: Install through APPS touching, or on the lines of, a water silo, a carbon dioxide store and a Cask ethanol tank, and connect its power point. Link them on its Control Panel, load a charge and Start; each charge takes an hour.
groups.find: Sold at the listed Manufacturing merchants and faction kiosks (Friendly standing); rare in engineering salvage.
groups.notes: New in Manufacturing 0.39.0; needs Phobos Agriculture 0.46.0 or newer for its feed. A working still lights ethanol spills in its room. 92% of the sugar ferments (authored, within published figures); the rest leaves as spent mash.

groups.title: Alembrine Corker-2 Bottling Unit
groups.function: A 2 x 2, 0.4 kW unit that draws ethanol from a Cask tank and water from a water silo and fills seven servings of Alembrine spirit at 40% alcohol a batch into its four-cell tray.
groups.use: Install through APPS touching, or on the lines of, a Cask ethanol tank and a water silo, and connect its power point. Link them on its Control Panel and Start; each half-hour batch takes 84.7 g of ethanol and 160.3 g of water. Take the spirit from its tray.
groups.find: Sold at the listed Manufacturing merchants and faction kiosks (Friendly standing); rare in engineering salvage.
groups.notes: New in Manufacturing 0.40.0. It keeps bottling while supplied and the tray has room, and carries on after a reload if it was running. The 0.2 kWh a batch is authored.

groups.title: Alembrine Cask-2, Cask-3 and Cask-4 Ethanol Tanks
groups.function: Bunded tanks for ethanol, kept as a kilogram record: 495 kg in the 2 x 2 Cask-2, with the 3 x 3 Cask-3 and 4 x 4 Cask-4 larger on the shared size ladder. Liquid tanks, not gas stores.
groups.use: Install through APPS touching the machines that will fill or draw from it, or join them with ethanol line laid under or right beside both. Pour ethanol into another cask it touches or shares an ethanol line with, from its panel or C1. Sell stored ethanol back at a station refuelling kiosk at 45%. Empty it before moving or dismantling it. Its four-place rack takes Framework drain canisters of ethanol.
groups.find: Sold at the listed supply merchants and faction kiosks (Friendly standing); found in engineering salvage like the other tanks. Stations never sell ethanol itself.
groups.notes: New in Manufacturing 0.38.0. Ethanol burns: a damaged cask offers a twentieth of its contents to a fire, which lights only with 5 kPa of oxygen and an ignition source in the room (an open fire, a working still or hearth, a powered device at half damage); the bund keeps the rest. Nothing makes ethanol until the fermenter-still arrives.

groups.title: Alembrine ethanol line
groups.function: Steel line for ethanol between the Cask tanks and the machines that fill or draw from them. Every cask and machine it runs under or right beside joins one network; touching equipment joins without it.
groups.use: Lay it through INSTALL > HVAC on intact floor until it runs under or right beside each cask and machine. To take it up, right-click it and choose Drain line into canister with a Framework drain canister carried or within two tiles; the run closes until Return line to service.
groups.find: Sold new at the K-Leg supply kiosk and fixer, San Diego Halvorson and the Venus scrap kiosk in supply lots. Also sold for scrip at the CCRE and GalCon faction kiosks, at any standing.
groups.notes: New in Manufacturing 0.38.0. Holds about 0.39 kg of ethanol a tile. A damaged segment keeps its ethanol, and a share can burn if the room lets it. On screen it shares a lane with the furnace coolant conduit: lay the two on different tiles. Dismantling returns retained line waste.

groups.title: L2 Canister Filling Station
groups.function: A powered 2 x 2 booster that tops up standard O2, N2 and CO2 canisters and suit O2 bottles to a safe 99% of their rated pressure and stops, even at fast-forward. Empty into stores mode empties them back into bulk stores.
groups.use: Install through INSTALL > HVAC and power it from conduit. Put suit O2 bottles in its rack (Inventory), link canisters installed beside it, and link oxygen, nitrogen or carbon dioxide stores within one tile or along a gas line, switching each on. A linked canister can be set to Draw from it instead. Choose Fill or Empty into stores, then press Start. A fill that was running carries on after a reload. Right-click Keep suit bottles charged to have crew with the Haul duty bring loose bottles below 90% into the rack and start it; choose a destination store in the Crew panel for charged bottles.
groups.find: Buy loose hardware from the sellers below; it is late-game equipment with late-game prices. No fabrication recipe. About one engineering-loot roll in twenty yields a Fennmark machine, usually broken. Also sold for scrip at the CCRE and GalCon faction kiosks; they ask Friendly standing.
groups.notes: Draws 3 kW while working; the electricity pays for compressing the gas (about 0.06 kWh per kilogram of oxygen into a canister) and all of it ends as heat in the room. Hydrogen and methane cannot be bottled: the game has no canister for them.

groups.title: A2 Cabin Air Regulator
groups.function: A powered 2 x 2 valve and sensor unit that holds the room it stands in at an oxygen set point from a linked oxygen store, then at a pressure set point from a linked nitrogen store. It only adds gas.
groups.use: Install through INSTALL > HVAC in the room to look after and power it from conduit. Link an oxygen store and, for pressure, a nitrogen store within one tile or along a gas line, choose the set points and press Switch on. It keeps working after a reload.
groups.find: Buy loose hardware from the sellers below; it is late-game equipment with late-game prices. No fabrication recipe. About one engineering-loot roll in twenty yields a Fennmark machine, usually broken. Also sold for scrip at the CCRE and GalCon faction kiosks; they ask Friendly standing.
groups.notes: Up to 6 kg of oxygen and 12 kg of nitrogen an hour. It stops feeding a room below 10 kPa (open to space) and never lets oxygen pass 30% of the air. It never vents, scrubs carbon dioxide or cools: keep the scrubbers running.

groups.title: Slingwright RM-1 Reaction Mass Feeder
groups.function: A powered 1 x 1 grinder that turns remainders (slag, cakes, calcine, rejects, tailings, retained waste) into up to 60 kg of reaction mass, which the RCS thrusters burn like nitrogen, kilogram for kilogram.
groups.use: Install through INSTALL > HVAC on an RCS Intake Regulator's gas-input tile, where a gas canister would go, and connect power. Put remainders in its Inventory, or choose a bin or locker under Take feed from. It grinds by itself at 3 kW, 0.15 kWh a kilogram. Draw order sets whether it burns before or after the canisters. Throw the reaction mass overboard before dismantling.
groups.find: Buy loose hardware from the sellers below. No fabrication recipe. About one engineering-loot roll in twenty yields a Manufacturing machine, usually broken; see the exact offers below. Also sold for scrip at the CCRE and GalCon faction kiosks; they ask Friendly standing.
groups.notes: New in Manufacturing 0.43.0. It takes remainders only, never ore, scrap, gangue or a product. Not a gas canister: station refuelling never fills it. The energy and exhaust figures are authored.

groups.title: P1 RCS Propellant Manifold
groups.function: A passive 1 x 1 valve block that feeds the ship's RCS thrusters from Fennmark gas stores (hydrogen, methane, oxygen, nitrogen or carbon dioxide). Each gas pushes by its own worth: methane about 1.45 times nitrogen per kilogram, hydrogen about 3.7 times.
groups.use: Install through INSTALL > HVAC on an RCS Intake Regulator's gas-input tile, where a gas canister would go. Link up to four stores within one tile, or along a gas line that runs under or right beside both, switch each on, choose Manifold first or Canisters first, and switch the manifold on. Everything starts off.
groups.find: Buy loose hardware from the sellers below; it is late-game equipment with late-game prices. No fabrication recipe. About one engineering-loot roll in twenty yields a Fennmark machine, usually broken; see the exact offers below. The K-Leg fixer buys it back intact and the Venus scrap kiosk intact or broken. Also sold for scrip at the CCRE and GalCon faction kiosks; they ask Friendly standing.
groups.notes: Not a gas canister: station refuelling never fills it. Draws settle to the stores every couple of seconds and before a save. Auto Nav's fuel and delta-v readings count the stores in nitrogen-equivalent kilograms.

groups.title: Raw stock, nickel steel and carbon black
groups.function: Nickel-iron ingots (4 kg, cast meteoric iron: iron with a few percent of nickel), carbon stock (1 kg) and nickel steel ingots (4 kg) are the refinery's products. Four nickel-iron ingots with one carbon stock become four nickel steel ingots in the V4, with or without Shipbreaker; the coming machining centre consumes ingots. Carbon black (1 kg, Manufacturing 0.27.0) is cracked out of methane on a carbon stock bed, with hydrogen as the by-product; the V4 burns it with stored oxygen into carbon dioxide for grow rooms.
groups.use: Made in the V4. Carry, stack (ten per stack) and sell at any general buyer, or feed four nickel-iron ingots and one carbon stock back into the V4 for nickel steel. With a methane store and a hydrogen store linked to the V4, one carbon stock alone is a methane-cracking charge; with an oxygen store and a carbon dioxide store linked, one carbon black is a burning charge.
groups.find: Made in the V4 from meteoric iron and carbon ore. Never sold in shops.
groups.notes: Refining pays (owner decision, 1 October 2026): four nickel-iron ingots ($880) are worth about twice the $450 meteoric iron block, five carbon stock ($190) with its water about twice the $99 carbon ore, and four nickel steel ingots ($1,040) about 2.2 times the iron and carbon ore behind them. Nickel steel is not Shipbreaker's plain steel ingot ($25), which the F6 casts from scrap. Ingots and carbon already aboard take the new prices when a save loads. Scrap kiosks do not buy them, so they are never furnace or processor feed. Carbon black is worth 12 cr, kept low so methane made from bought water and carbon dioxide never pays its way back as soot.

groups.title: Fertiliser salts and intermediates
groups.function: Potassium sulfate (0.70 kg), struvite (0.43 kg, slow-release magnesium ammonium phosphate), Epsom salt (0.432 kg of magnesium sulfate from olivine) and ammonium sulfate (0.232 kg, from the struvite from acid) are fertiliser salts; phosphate concentrate (0.25 kg) is struvite's feed; a leached residue (6.8 kg of washed clay and magnesium carbonate) is the V4's calcine feed.
groups.use: Made in the LC-3. Put a phosphate concentrate back in the LC-3 for struvite, or a phosphoric acid flask with three Epsom salt for struvite and ammonium sulfate; blend one potassium sulfate with two struvite for Groundwork makeup salts, or one of each of the four salts into crop nutrients for a nutrient hopper (with Agriculture); calcine a leached residue in the V4 for carbon dioxide. Sell the salts at any general buyer.
groups.find: Made in the LC-3 from mined evaporite crust, the game's olivine and the SA-3's phosphoric acid. Never sold in shops.
groups.notes: Refining pays (owner decision, 1 October 2026): potassium sulfate 190 cr, phosphate concentrate 110 cr, struvite 125 cr, Epsom salt 13 cr and ammonium sulfate 20 cr, so leaching a crust earns about twice the crust and an olivine about 2.3 times the ore; the leached residue is priced as trash because the V4 takes it. The makeup salts are worth Agriculture's own 30 cr a packet, and crop nutrients its 1,500 cr/kg (bag a hopper's nutrients into bulk charges to sell them; the station does not buy them back from a hopper). Salts already aboard take the new prices when a save loads.

groups.title: Ferrosilicon
groups.function: 2.2 kg of iron-silicon metal (1.414 kg of iron, 0.786 kg of silicon) tapped from an Oxsmith EC-4 or CR-4: three from a regolith lump, two from a Silicates ore chunk.
groups.use: Choose hydrogen from ferrosilicon on an LC-3 with a hydrogen store and a water vessel linked, and load three: 3.02 kg of water becomes 0.339 kg of hydrogen in the store, leaving three spent ferrosilicon. It can also be sold, for very little.
groups.find: Made in the EC-4 or the CR-4. Never sold in shops.
groups.notes: Priced at 2 cr so that a regolith lump's oxygen, water and ferrosilicon sold back never repay the lump a prospector sells. The hydrogen recipe follows the silicol process, which really consumes caustic soda; ours keeps its caustic in the machine, an authored simplification.

groups.title: Phosphoric acid flask
groups.function: 0.515 kg of phosphoric acid caught from a roasted nodule, in a sealed flask: the phosphorus of three struvite units.
groups.use: Made in the SA-3. The LC-3's struvite from acid takes one with three Epsom salt. Carry, stack (ten per stack) and sell at any general buyer.
groups.find: Made in the SA-3 from sulfide nodules. Never sold in shops.
groups.notes: Priced at 300 cr, so roasting a nodule earns about twice the nodule (owner decision, 1 October 2026). Flasks already aboard take the new price when a save loads.

groups.title: Alembrine spirit
groups.function: A 35 g serving of clear spirit at 40% alcohol by volume, bottled aboard from your own ethanol. Crew drink it like the game's own liquor, with the same effects.
groups.use: Leave it where crew can reach it, or sell it to the game's buyers. It stacks seven to a batch.
groups.find: Made in the Corker-2 bottling unit. Never sold in shops.
groups.notes: Priced at 8 cr a serving (owner decision, 4 October 2026: an own-brand spirit in the refining band), so a sugar beet rack's ethanol bottles into about twice the crop's nutrients and water. A copy of the game's vodka serving with its own name and price.

groups.title: Regolith paver and sintered regolith floor
groups.function: A 6.5 kg slab of sintered regolith, and the floor a crew member lays from it. The floor is our own twin of the stations' Polished Regolith Floor: the same picture and figures, covering a 2 x 2 patch, and floor to pipes, belts and machines.
groups.use: Set a V4's Loose regolith choice to Regolith pavers and give it a lump: three pavers come out. Lay one from INSTALL, under hull, with a welder; lift it again with a structure cutter, which gives the paver back.
groups.find: Pavers are made in the V4 from loose regolith. Never sold in shops. The floor is only ever laid by your crew.
groups.notes: A paver is 13 cr, below the floor's 21: a prospector sells regolith, so three pavers earn at most a quarter more than the lump. A save with this floor laid needs Phobos Manufacturing kept installed; removing the mod leaves holes where it lay. Until the paver has its own art it shows the game's loose floor plate picture.

groups.title: Terminal remainders
groups.function: Refinery slag (1 kg: sulfide, phosphide and oxide skimmings, or a frozen melt), anhydrous residue (8 kg of baked clay minerals), spent salt cake (7.305 kg of table salt baked into clay), brine salt cake (2.25 kg of the evaporite crust's sodium salts), caustic remainder (70 g of sodium hydroxide from struvite), calcined residue (6.54 kg of baked clay and magnesia), roasted calcine (9.535 kg of iron and nickel oxides and rock from the SA-3), olivine leach cake (14.33 kg of silica gel, iron sulfate, rock and Epsom liquor from the LC-3), exhausted sorbent (2.5 kg: the one CO2 filter in four that reactivation in the V4 cannot bring back), plant ash (30 g: the minerals of one burned or charred straw bale) spent mash (0.5 kg: what a fermenter-still charge leaves) and washed tailings (1 kg units, one stack a wash: what the LC-3's acid leaves of gangue). Trash at the technical minimum price; nothing recovers them. Baked regolith (19.5 kg: a regolith lump with its water baked out by the V4) keeps the game's regolith picture. Spent ferrosilicon (3.095 kg: the iron fines and silica the LC-3 leaves of a ferrosilicon unit once its silicon has made hydrogen) is the newest. The EC-4 and the CR-4 also leave refinery slag.
groups.use: Feed them to a Slingwright RM-1 reaction mass feeder, which grinds them into thrust for the RCS. They can still be sold or discarded.
groups.find: Left in the V4, LC-3, SA-3, EC-4, CR-4 or fermenter-still inventory by their charges. Never sold.
groups.notes: Terminal: never re-processed, never the game's own Trash item.

groups.title: Clay hydrates
groups.function: A 10 kg chunk of dark, water-rich clay minerals of the kind sampled from carbonaceous asteroids, about a fifth of it bound water.
groups.use: Bake it in the V4 for 2 kg of water and an 8 kg residue, or sell it to a government kiosk like other ore.
groups.find: Mined: C-class deposits and dark regolith walls turn it up in place of some of the silicates they would otherwise give: about one pull in eleven from a C-class deposit, far fewer from walls. Never sold.
groups.notes: Authored from the CI-chondrite range (18 to 22 percent water by weight) with the game's own hydrate art until its own sprite exists.

groups.title: Ammonium salt crust
groups.function: A 10 kg chunk of pale salt crust: ammonium chloride with sodium carbonate and clay, like the bright salt deposits NASA's Dawn mission found on Ceres. The ship's only mined source of nitrogen.
groups.use: Bake it in the V4 with an ammonia store linked: 0.955 kg of ammonia to the store, 0.505 kg of water to the linked vessel, 1.235 kg of carbon dioxide into the room and a 7.305 kg spent salt cake in the tray. Or sell it to a government kiosk like other ore.
groups.find: Mined: C-class deposits and dark regolith walls turn it up in place of some of the silicates they would otherwise give: about one pull in twenty-one from a C-class deposit, far fewer from walls. Never sold.
groups.notes: The mix (30 percent ammonium chloride) is authored from the Dawn findings; see the chemistry record for sources and the rounding.

groups.title: Evaporite crust
groups.function: A 10 kg chunk of salt-streaked clay from a dried brine vein: rock salt, potassium chloride, sodium sulfate and carbonate, a little magnesium phosphate and a trace of fluoride salt, the minerals NASA's OSIRIS-REx team reported in samples from the asteroid Bennu.
groups.use: Leach it in the LC-3 for potassium sulfate, phosphate concentrate, a leached residue and a brine salt cake, or sell it to a government kiosk like other ore.
groups.find: Mined: C-class deposits and dark regolith walls turn it up in place of some of the silicates they would otherwise give: about one pull in twenty-one from a C-class deposit, far fewer from walls. Never sold.
groups.notes: The minerals follow McCoy et al. 2025 (Nature); the paper gives no bulk fractions, so the proportions (0.60 kg of potassium chloride per chunk, for example) are authored. See the chemistry record for sources and the rounding.

groups.title: Sulfide nodule
groups.function: A 10 kg chunk of troilite (iron sulfide) with schreibersite, a nickel-iron phosphide, of the kind found in iron meteorites. The ship's source of sulfur and phosphorus.
groups.use: Roast it in an SA-3 for sulfuric acid and a phosphoric acid flask, or sell it to a government kiosk like other ore.
groups.find: Mined: M-class and S-class deposits turn it up in place of some of their meteoric iron, about one pull in thirty-six from an M-class deposit and one in sixty-three from an S-class one. Never sold.
groups.notes: The mix (7.000 kg troilite, 1.058 kg phosphide, 1.942 kg rock) is authored after Buchwald's handbook of iron meteorites; see the chemistry record.

groups.title: Built-in charge feeds
groups.function: The V4's, the LC-3's, the SA-3's, the fermenter-still's, the EC-4's and the CR-4's charge feeds, named child inventories built into the machines. Not separate products.
groups.use: Put the charge in the machine's Inventory and press Start: the machine takes one exact charge into this compartment and Cancel puts it back. The V4 takes single ore blocks, clay chunks, salt crusts, leached residues, nickel-iron ingots or carbon stock; the LC-3 takes only the chosen recipe's feed (an evaporite crust, a phosphate concentrate, or potassium sulfate and struvite). The SA-3 takes sulfide nodules only; the fermenter-still takes six sugar beets or six beet sugar packets. The EC-4 and the CR-4 each take one lump of loose regolith or one chunk of Silicates ore. Each binds one exact charge at a time.
groups.find: Inside the V4, the LC-3, the SA-3, the fermenter-still, the EC-4 or the CR-4; the game does not show it as a window.
groups.notes: No purchase, INSTALL, repair, Restore or standalone salvage contract.

groups.title: Gas fire
groups.function: The game's own explosion objects in three sizes, spawned for a moment when a damaged or destroyed fuel store (hydrogen or methane) or a damaged reactor's hydrogen burns. Not items.
groups.use: Not usable. They apply the game's radius damage, shrapnel and fire rolls and remove themselves.
groups.find: Only where stored fuel burns.
groups.notes: Their entries live in the mod's data/explosions file.

PhobosWarDeclared.intro: Phobos' War Has Been Declared adds no items, equipment or recipes. It adds three orders to the game's own navigation stations (Battle stations, Stand down and Lay postponed build sites) and lays the game's own build sites for parts destroyed in battle, which the crew finish with ordinary replacement parts. See [the player guide](war-declared-player-guide.md).

PhobosMedical.intro: Phobos Medical adds the Halewright Ward-3 Medical Bed, a powered sickbay bed that takes an unconscious casualty, lets the injured rest awake, and keeps its patient recuperating with the game's own medical-rest healing while it has power and air. Crew can be set to dress, splint and re-dress whoever lies in it. The Halewright Vigil-2 Patient Monitor stands beside a Ward-3 and shows its patient's readings and alerts. See [the player guide](medical-player-guide.md).

groups.title: Ward-3 Medical Bed
groups.function: A 3 x 5 powered medical bed. While installed, intact, powered and in a room with air, its patient recuperates: the game's own medical-rest healing (wound, blood and infection recovery and pain threshold), the same as the vanilla Infirmaway gives a sleeper. Without power or air it is an ordinary bed. A 3 x 2 drawer holds dressings, splints and medicines; Keep patient treated draws its supplies from it.
groups.use: Install through FURN with its head against a wall carrying power. Drag an unconscious person to it and choose Lay patient here; order an injured crew member to Rest and recover; or Sleep in it when tired. Switch on Send injured crew here and a free bed calls the worst-off injured crew member. Switch on Keep patient treated and crew dress bleeding wounds, splint broken bones and change dirty dressings on its patient with cloth and splints from the drawer, fetching more from around the ship. The Control Panel shows the patient and a short health reading, and sets whether anyone may sleep in it or only the injured. 22.5 W idle, 150 W while caring.
groups.find: Buy loose hardware from the sellers below: new at the K-Leg furnishings kiosk, worn from the K-Leg fixer, broken at the K-Leg supply kiosk, refurbished at the Venus scrap kiosk, and at the regional supply kiosks. About one engineering-loot roll in fifty yields a Ward-3, usually broken. Also sold for scrip at the CCRE and GalCon faction kiosks; they ask Friendly standing.
groups.notes: Its treatment cartridges and folded arms are 2075 styling; the healing is the game's own medical rest. Uninstalling or dismantling is refused while someone is in it. Under its care a weightless patient heals at the normal rate (the game otherwise slows it to a twentieth). It does not dress wounds yet.

groups.title: Vigil-2 Patient Monitor
groups.function: A 2 x 2 bedside monitor cart. It watches the patient of the Ward-3 it touches and shows blood lost, infection, pain and every wound with the change over the last hour, and posts a caution when a figure rises to its alert level or a wound starts bleeding. It never treats or heals. It stores nothing.
groups.use: Install through APPS beside a Ward-3, touching it or one tile away, with its back against a wall carrying power. Open its Control Panel for the readings; set which touching bed it watches and whether it posts alerts. 10 W idle, 60 W while watching.
groups.find: Buy loose hardware from the sellers below, on the Ward-3's routes. A rare engineering-loot find, usually broken. Also sold for scrip at the CCRE and GalCon faction kiosks; they ask Warm standing.
groups.notes: Its hour's trend is kept in memory and starts again after a reload. Readings it cannot take say so rather than showing zero.

PhobosSpacerStories.intro: Phobos Spacer Stories adds no equipment or recipes. It is a data-only story collection about vanilla station life and Phobos makers: TV news and adverts, crew talk, loading lore, encyclopedia articles and 22 chains with 23 readable archive files. Files arrive on the game's Renbao R014 Data Cards and can be read on any computer or PDA. New local stories have no expiry; one optional letter waits for a convenient trip to Titan. Two once-only fees total 900 credits; no new chain takes money or goods. Vanilla gigs are unchanged. See [writing story content](writing-story-content.md) and the [expansion record](development/spacer-stories-vanilla-expansion.md).

PhobosBank.intro: Phobos Banking adds no items, equipment or recipes. It adds the CREDIT app to the PDA home screen, which lists what you owe from the game's own ledger (loans and mortgages, bills to pay and regular charges), lets you borrow from lenders where you are or finance a ship or apartment at the broker, and opens the game's Finances window, where bills are paid. Lenders are a data file you can extend. See [the player guide](bank-player-guide.md).
